newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey's army to keep up anti-Islamist campaign.
newsitem.headline: Turkey's army to keep up anti-Islamist campaign.

text.p: Turkey's staunchly secularist military said on Thursday it would press ahead with its anti-Islamist campaign despite the resignation of Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan.
"The mission of the Turkish armed forces of protecting the Turkish republic's unity against the threat of fundamentalism is still valid and continuing," a senior military official told Reuters.
"It must not be linked with the recent political developments," he added.
Erbakan resigned on Wednesday after a fierce row between the ruling Islamists and the powerful army over rising religious sentiment in public life.
The row erupted publicly in February when an army-dominated council demanded an anti-Islamist crackdown.
The generals, who see themselves as the guardians of Turkey's 73-year official secularism, called on all citizens to fight the danger of Moslem activism during a briefing for journalists last week
They accused Erbakan of threatening the secular order by promoting Islamic groups, among which they said were militant elements.

"The opinions conveyed in the briefing are still valid," the army official said. Security officials, inspired by the army, have closed down dozens of illegal religious education centres and a prosecutor has filed a case at the constitutional court to have Erbakan's Islam-based Welfare Party banned.
Four members of a Germany-based Turkish Islamic group have been arrested in the western province of Aydin, Anatolian news agency said.

The four, detained on Monday, confessed to having been active followers of the late Cemalettin Kaplan, a fiery Turkish preacher who died in Germany in 1995. Kaplan had vowed to set up a strictly Islamic state in Turkey.
Demirel on Thursday began to meet party leaders to replace Erbakan's government, which fell after a year it was set up.
Erbakan, his secularist coalition partner Tansu Ciller and a far-right leader proposed a plan to Demirel on Wednesday to form a caretaker coalition to take the country to early elections.
